Subject: Evaluating upgrade path (Compact -> Elastic) and proration questions

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We're close to deciding whether to move our production routing over to Redwood's Elastic tier, but I need a clearer mapping of what exactly changes between our current Compact package and Elastic. Two specific asks:

1) Feature mapping: which entitlements in Compact have exact parity in Elastic and which are additive (e.g., KV cache premium, streaming concurrency, per-route caching). A simple table would be ideal.

2) Billing/proration: If we upgrade mid-billing-cycle, how will seats and committed tokens be prorated? Also want to understand what one-time credits or onboarding grants you might offer for a 12-month commit.

I attached our July usage export so you can see our burst patterns.

Also looping in Samir from procurement so he can track the numbers.

Can you get a short mapping + proration example over today or tomorrow? We have an internal exec sync Friday and I'd like to have numbers.

Thanks,
Mila

Mila Kwon
Head of Platform Engineering, HealthBridge
M: 415-555-9831

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-08-30T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluating upgrade path (Compact -> Elastic) and proration questions

Hi Mila — thanks for the clear asks and for sending the usage file. Attached is a first-pass "upgrade_matrix.csv" that maps Compact entitlements to Elastic equivalents and flags additive features. Highlights:

- Most API-level features are parity (text generation, embeddings, standard streaming).
- Elastic includes the "KV cache premium" and a higher default continuous-batching window — those are additive and drive token-efficiency for high-concurrency bursts.
- Per-route caching is available in both but Elastic supports route-level TTLs and higher cache size by default (Compact requires optional add-on).

Proration approach (short example):
- Seats: pro-rated by days remaining in current billing month.
- Committed tokens: if you upgrade mid-cycle we spread the remaining committed tokens' value proportionally and then rebase to the Elastic committed rate; any delta becomes either billed or credited at the end of the month depending on usage.

Commercial offer: for a 12-month committed term we can provide a one-time onboarding credit equal to one month of your average committed spend (applied as account credit on first invoice) and waive the first-month seat-change fee. That is contingent on signing the amendment before Sept 15.

I've looped in Ben for technical mapping confirmations and Lauren for a final proration calc based on your attached CSV. If you want, we can also provide a quick prorate calculator sheet for exact numbers.

Next steps: Ben will reply with a technical margin / latency note. Lauren will send the prorate example and final paper. If that looks good, I'll prepare the amendment and DocuSign.

Best,
Rafael

--
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Evaluating upgrade path (Compact -> Elastic) and proration questions

Mila / Rafael — quick follow-up from engineering side. I reviewed the July usage file and sketched an operational mapping. Key technical notes:

- KV cache premium: Elastic's implementation increases effective context reuse for short-turn workloads by ~12-18% in our tests. If you migrate, you should expect lower token egress cost for chat-like flows (we've reflected expected delta in the matrix).

- Streaming concurrency: Compact has a 4-stream soft limit; Elastic defaults to 16. For your peak bursts (seen 120 concurrent connections in the CSV) we recommend a phased ramp — keep most steady-state traffic on Compact routes while gradually moving high-throughput routes to Elastic. That avoids cold-cache penalties.

- Feature gating: we can enable per-route TTLs and incremental KV tiers per route. My suggestion is a 3-week pilot where we migrate 20% of requests (the top 5 routes by volume) to Elastic, measure token-cost delta and latency, then scale.

I've attached a short tech note and the upgrade_matrix.csv with per-feature rows and notes. Rafael — if we offer the 3-week pilot and provide a one-time credit to offset onboarding token churn, that's likely to make the exec decision easier.

On quoting the earlier email:
> On Aug 30, 2026, at 11:05 AM, Rafael Mendes wrote:

>
Happy to jump on a 20-minute call to walk the team through the matrix.

-ben
